newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada agency says fusarium in two pct of wheat.
newsitem.headline: Canada agency says fusarium in two pct of wheat.

text.p: Two percent of early harvest samples taken in the eastern Prairie province of Manitoba showed minor downgrading levels of fusarium head blight in wheat, a Canadian Grain Commission official told Reuters.

"Manitoba's fusarium is fairly prevalent at one to two percent of what's been harvested. A lot of those samples are being downgraded to No2 (Canada Western) Red (Spring Wheat) from No1," CGC acting chief grain inspector David Samson said.
The estimate was based on 3,500 samples of grain taken across the Prairies. Grain standards are set in November by a committee of farmers and industry officials on 25,000 samples.
"In southeast Saskatchewan, (wheat) midge damage downgraded samples to No 3 Red from No1. The midge damage is limited to certain areas and southeast Saskatchewan is one of them," Samson said.
There was no preliminary estimate of the proportion of the wheat crop damaged by wheat midge, an insect.
"There's small pockets of ergot in Saskatchewan and some fusarium in southeast Saskatchewan," Samson added.
Ergot is a fungus that strikes cereals in the flowering stage.
"Alberta's looking pretty good so far," Samson said.
